english: I'm going on an overseas trip next month.
grammar: 해외 (haeoe) = overseas: 해외여행 = trip abroad, 국내 여행 = domestic trip.

english: I got my passport ready in advance.
I arrived at the airport three hours early.
grammar: Hours of duration use native numbers: 세 시간 (se sigan) = three hours.

english: Where do I check in?
Please show your boarding pass here.
grammar: 보여 주세요 (boyeo juseyo) = please show me — 보이다 + 주다.

english: My luggage is heavier than I thought.
grammar: 무겁다 flips ㅂ to 우: 무거워요 (mugeowoyo) = is heavy.

english: How many kilos of baggage are allowed?
A window seat, please.
grammar: (으)로 marks the choice: 창가 자리로 (changga jariro) = as a window seat.

english: An aisle seat is more comfortable.
I'm not sure where the gate is.
grammar: -ㄴ지 embeds a question: 어디인지 (eodi-inji) = where it is.

english: The flight was delayed two hours.
I got through departure screening quickly.
I bought cosmetics at the duty-free shop.
Please fasten your seatbelt.

target: 이 짐은 기내에 들고 탈 거예요.
english: I'll carry this bag on board.
grammar: 들고 타다 = carry on: 들고 탈 거예요 = will carry it aboard.

english: The layover time is plenty.
I transferred to the next flight.
grammar: 갈아타다 = to transfer: 갈아탔어요 (garatasseoyo) = changed transport.

english: I'm going to Paris via a connection.
The flight took twelve hours.
The in-flight meal was tastier than expected.
I stood in line a long time at immigration.
What is the purpose of your visit?
I came to do some sightseeing.
grammar: -러 marks purpose of going: 관광하러 (gwangwanghareo) = in order to sightsee.

english: How long will you stay?
I'll be here about a week.
grammar: 정도 (jeongdo) = about, roughly: 일주일 정도 = about a week.

english: I'll be staying at a hotel.
Please scan your fingerprint here.
I filled out the arrival card in advance.
They opened my bag at customs.
I have nothing to declare.
Where is baggage claim?
grammar: -는 곳 = the place where: 짐을 찾는 곳 (channeun got) = baggage claim.

english: My baggage hasn't come out yet.
grammar: 아직 안 = not yet: 아직 안 나왔어요 (ajik an nawasseoyo).

english: I bought a SIM card at the airport.
Where do I exchange money?
I took the airport bus into the city.
I applied for a visa.
I came on a tourist visa.
I need a student visa.
You can go to Korea visa-free.
grammar: 무비자 (mubija) = visa-free: 무- means "without".

english: I'd like to extend my visa.
I submitted documents to the embassy.
The visa comes out next week.
My passport expires soon.
The visa is valid for three months.
grammar: Months of duration use Sino numbers: 삼 개월 (sam gaewol) = 3 months.

english: I searched for the consulate location.
I'm missing one document.
I took new visa photos.
I'll go study a language abroad next year.
grammar: 어학연수 (eohangyeonsu) = language study abroad.

english: I came to Seoul to study.
grammar: 유학 (yuhak) = studying abroad: 유학을 왔어요 = came to study.

english: I enrolled at a language school.
I'll study for one semester.
grammar: 동안 = for a duration: 한 학기 동안 = for one semester.

english: The tuition is a bit expensive.
I took the placement test.
I got into the intermediate class.
grammar: 중급 (junggeup) = intermediate level; 초급 = beginner, 고급 = advanced.

english: I live in a dormitory.
My homestay family is really kind.
My host mother cooks well.
grammar: Elders take -세요: 잘하세요 (jalhaseyo) shows respect.

english: I came as an exchange student.
Class starts at nine in the morning.
grammar: Clock hours use native numbers: 아홉 시 (ahop si) = nine oclock.

english: There's a lot of homework every day.
The speaking test is the hardest.
I made a lot of Korean friends.
I study at the library after class.
grammar: 후에 = after: 수업 후에 (sueop hue) = after class.

english: My pronunciation has improved a lot.
The teacher speaks slowly.
grammar: 말씀하시다 = to speak (honorific): 말씀하세요 for a teacher.

english: I want to get a scholarship.
I'll travel around during the break.
I'm preparing for the Korean proficiency test.
I'm gradually getting used to local life.
grammar: 익숙해지다 = to get used to: 익숙해져요 (iksukaejyeoyo).

english: I received a certificate of completion.
I'll register for next semester too.
grammar: -(으)ㄹ게요 is a promise: 등록할게요 (deungnokalgeyo) = I will register.

english: I get along well with my roommate.
At first I had culture shock.
grammar: 문화충격 (munhwachunggyeok) = culture shock: 충격을 받다 = be shocked.

english: There is a tipping culture here.
The culture is very different from Korea's.
grammar: 와/과 다르다 = different from: 한국하고 달라요 (dallayo).

english: Table manners differ from ours.
The way people greet is different.
grammar: -는 방법 = the way of: 인사하는 방법 = way of greeting.

english: I don't know this country's customs well.
At first everything felt unfamiliar.
Now I've gotten quite used to it.
People here are really friendly.
I was surprised the shops close early.
grammar: -아서 gives a cause: 닫아서 (dadaseo) = because it closes.

english: The local food suits my taste well.
grammar: 입에 맞다 = to suit ones taste: 입에 맞아요 (ibe majayo).

english: Sometimes I miss spicy food.
grammar: 그립다 flips ㅂ to 우: 그리워요 (geuriwoyo) = I miss it.

english: The weather is the opposite of Korea's.
Life abroad is harder than I thought.
I felt frustrated because I couldn't communicate.
grammar: 말이 통하다 = to communicate: 안 통해서 = because it doesnt get through.

english: I barely explained with gestures.
A local friend helped me a lot.
I got lost because I didn't know how to take the bus.

target: 시차 때문에 밤에 잠이 안 와요.
english: I can't sleep at night because of jet lag.
grammar: 시차 (sicha) = time difference/jet lag: 시차 때문에 = because of jet lag.

english: Prices are higher than in Korea.
This city feels comfortable to me now.
I met friends from various countries.
My homesickness is bad these days.
grammar: 향수병 (hyangsubyeong) = homesickness (lit. nostalgia illness).

english: I really miss my family.
grammar: 보고 싶다 = to miss (a person): 보고 싶어요 (bogo sipeoyo).

english: I video-call my parents every day.
My mom misses me a lot.
grammar: 3rd-person feelings take -어하다: 그리워하세요 (geuriwohaseyo) = (she) misses.

english: My younger sibling wonders how I am.
grammar: Others' curiosity uses -어하다: 궁금해해요 (gunggeumhaehaeyo).

english: I keep thinking of Korean food.
When I miss home, I look at photos.
grammar: -(으)ㄹ 때 = when: 그리울 때 (geuriul ttae) = when I miss it.

english: I feel lonely when I'm alone at night.
My friends worry about me.
Hearing my parents' voices gives me strength.
grammar: 들으면: 듣다 is ㄷ-irregular — 들으면 (deureumyeon) = if/when I hear.

english: I put a family photo on my desk.
I make sure to watch Korean news every day.
grammar: 챙겨 보다 = to make a point of watching: 챙겨 봐요.

english: I miss my family especially on holidays.
grammar: 명절 (myeongjeol) = traditional holiday.

english: I want to eat the kimchi stew my mom makes.
grammar: -고 싶다 = to want to: 먹고 싶어요 (meokgo sipeoyo).

english: A friend sent me a package.
As time passed it got a little better.
grammar: -(으)니까 = as/since: 지나니까 (jinanikka) = as time passes.

english: I bought ramen at the Korean grocery store.
My family says they'll come visit soon.
grammar: -ㄴ대요 relays what was said: 온대요 (ondaeyo) = (they) say they'll come.

english: It took time to adjust.
grammar: -는 데 = for the task of: 적응하는 데 (jeogeunghaneun de) = to adjust.

english: Now this place feels like a second home.

target: 방학에 한국에 갈 생각을 하면 설레요.
english: I get excited thinking about going to Korea on break.
I write letters to my parents often.
grammar: 께 is the honorific 에게: 부모님께 (bumonimkke) = to (my) parents.

english: Whenever things are hard I think of my family.
grammar: -ㄹ 때마다 = every time: 힘들 때마다 (himdeul ttaemada).

english: They weighed my bag when I checked it in.

target: 비상구 좌석은 다리를 뻗을 수 있어요.
english: Emergency-exit seats let you stretch your legs.
I slept the whole flight.
I got an entry stamp in my passport.
I rented a car at the airport.
A local SIM is much cheaper.
I was very nervous since it was my first trip abroad.
grammar: -이라서 = because it is: 첫 여행이라서 (yeohaeng-iraseo).

english: I rested briefly in the airport lounge.
In my opinion, that is right.
grammar: 제 생각에는 (je saenggageneun) = in my opinion — a soft opinion opener.

english: I don't necessarily think so.
grammar: -지 않다 negates: 생각하지 않아요 (saenggakaji anayo) = I dont think so.

english: I think this plan is good.
grammar: ~다고 생각해요 = I think that ~: 좋다고 생각해요 (jotago saenggakaeyo).

english: I think that is correct.
grammar: ~것 같아요 softens a claim: 맞는 것 같아요 (manneun geot gatayo) = seems right.

english: My opinion is a bit different from that.
grammar: 의견 (uigyeon) = opinion: 제 의견은 = my opinion is.

english: Personally, I'm against it.
Honestly, I'm not sure.
grammar: 솔직히 말하면 (soljikhi malhamyeon) = to be honest.

english: The way I see it, there is a problem.
That opinion makes sense.
grammar: 일리가 있다 = to have a point: 일리가 있어요 (illiga isseoyo).

english: This differs from person to person.
I think the same.
I'm not certain, but it's probably so.
grammar: -지는 않지만 = not quite, but: 확실하지는 않지만.

english: I'll share my honest opinion.
I'll give it some thought.
grammar: -아/어 볼게요 = I will try: 생각해 볼게요 (saenggakae bolgeyo).

english: I admit that point too.
From my position, it doesn't make sense.
grammar: 입장 (ipjang) = position/stance: 제 입장에서는 = from my standpoint.

target: 이 문제는 좀 더 고민해야 해요.
english: We need to think this over more.
grammar: -아야 하다 = must: 고민해야 해요 (gominhaeya haeyo) = must ponder.

english: Many people feel that way.
I have my own reasons.
That depends on the situation.
grammar: -에 따라 = depending on: 상황에 따라 (sanghwange ttara).

english: I agree with the part you mentioned.
My conclusion is this.
I support that opinion.
grammar: 찬성하다 = to be in favor: 찬성해요 (chanseonghaeyo) = I agree/support.

english: I'm against that plan.
grammar: 반대하다 = to oppose: 반대해요 (bandaehaeyo) = I object.

english: I completely agree with that.
grammar: 동의하다 = to agree: 완전히 동의해요 (wanjeonhi dongihaeyo).

english: I think so too.
I'd like to object to that point.
It's right to some degree.
grammar: 어느 정도 (eoneu jeongdo) = to some extent.

english: I don't think that's quite right.
grammar: 아닌 것 같아요 = seems not so — a polite disagreement.

english: There are more people in favor.
I want to hear the reasons against.
It's not that I oppose that opinion.
grammar: -는 건 아니에요 = its not that: softens the stance.

english: I only partly agree.
I respect that view too.
We can think differently from each other.
grammar: 서로 (seoro) = each other; -(으)ㄹ 수 있다 = can.

english: I'm a bit skeptical of that opinion.
Opinions split evenly for and against.
grammar: 찬반 (chanban) = pro and con: 찬반으로 갈리다 = split into for/against.

english: It'd be best to follow the majority view.

target: 근거를 들면 이렇게 설명할 수 있어요.
english: To give grounds, I can explain it this way.
grammar: 근거를 들다 = to cite grounds: 근거를 들면 (geungeoreul deulmyeon).

english: For example, there are cases like this.
grammar: 예를 들면 (yereul deulmyeon) = for example.

english: It's because there isn't enough time.
grammar: 왜냐하면 ~기 때문에 = because: 부족하기 때문이에요.

english: First, it costs too much.
grammar: 첫째 (cheotjjae) = firstly: 첫째로 = first of all.

english: Second, it also takes a long time.
According to statistics, that isn't so.
grammar: -에 따르면 = according to: 통계에 따르면 (tonggye-e ttareumyeon).

english: Research results show that.
It's clear when you look at the data.
A concrete example is needed.
I'm speaking based on my experience.
grammar: -을 근거로 = based on: 경험을 근거로 (gyeongheomeul geungeoro).

english: There are broadly two reasons.
That claim lacks evidence.
Experts say the same thing too.
We should check the facts first.
You shouldn't speak without grounds.
grammar: -면 안 되다 = must not: 말하면 안 돼요 (malhamyeon an dwaeyo).

english: I think environmental issues are the most important.
We should recycle more diligently.
We should reduce plastic use.
Technology has changed our lives.
I worry AI might cut jobs.
grammar: -(으)ㄹ까 봐 = worried that: 줄일까 봐 (juril-kka bwa).

english: It's hard to live without a smartphone.
grammar: 없이는 = without: 스마트폰 없이는 (seumateupon eopsineun).

english: Social media has pros and cons.

target: 소셜미디어를 너무 많이 하면 안 좋아요.
english: It's not good to overuse social media.
I think the education system should change.
Exam-centered education is a problem.
grammar: 위주 (wiju) = -centered: 시험 위주 = exam-focused.

english: Working from home is more efficient.
grammar: 재택근무 (jaetaekgeunmu) = remote work; 효율적 = efficient.

english: Remote work has downsides too.
I think city life is more convenient.
The countryside is nicer to live in than the city.
grammar: 살기 좋다 = good to live in: 살기 좋아요 (salgi joayo).

english: It's good to use public transport.
Work-life balance is really important.
grammar: 워라밸 (worabael) = work-life balance — a clipped loanword.

english: The younger generation thinks differently.
Online classes have many advantages too.
Health is more important than money.
Exercise helps relieve stress.
Reading develops thinking skills.
Learning a foreign language broadens your view.
Cutting disposables is good for the environment.
Electric cars will grow more common in the future.

target: 가짜 뉴스가 사회에 나쁜 영향을 줘요.
english: Fake news has a bad influence on society.
grammar: 영향을 주다 = to influence: 영향을 줘요 (yeonghyangeul jwoyo).

english: You shouldn't just believe information as is.
Don't trust ads too much.
grammar: -지 마세요 = please dont: 믿지 마세요 (mitji maseyo).

english: I think low birth rates are a serious problem.
I'm worried because housing is too expensive.
Volunteering helps society.
But we should look at the other side too.
grammar: 하지만 (hajiman) = but, however — starts a contrast.

english: On the other hand, there are these problems too.
grammar: 반면에 (banmyeone) = on the other hand.

english: Still, I tend to be in favor.
grammar: -는 편이다 = tend to: 찬성하는 편이에요 (chanseonghaneun pyeonieyo).

english: Of course there are downsides, but it's fine.
In a way, both are right.
grammar: 어떻게 보면 (eotteoke bomyeon) = in a sense.

english: You can't necessarily say that's so.
grammar: 꼭 ~ 것은 아니다 = not necessarily: 꼭 그렇다고 볼 수 없어요.

english: Neither side is perfect.
On reflection, I was wrong.
grammar: -아 보니 = upon doing: 생각해 보니 (saenggakae boni) = now that I think.

english: I hadn't thought of that point.
Now that I hear it, it makes sense.
grammar: -고 보니 = after doing: 듣고 보니 (deutgo boni).

english: I opposed it at first, but now I agree.
I hope we each give a little.
In conclusion, I support this proposal.
grammar: 결론적으로 (gyeolloncheogeuro) = in conclusion.

english: To summarize, two things are key.
grammar: 요약하면 (yoyakamyeon) = to summarize; 핵심 = the crux.

english: In other words, we need more time.
grammar: 다시 말하면 (dasi malhamyeon) = in other words.

english: To put it in order, it comes to this.
In the end the choice is up to each person.

target: 이 정도면 충분히 설명한 것 같아요.
english: I think that explains it well enough.
grammar: 이 정도면 = at this level: 이 정도면 충분해요 = this much is enough.

english: Lastly, I'll add just one thing.
grammar: 끝으로 (kkeuteuro) = lastly; 덧붙이다 = to add on.

english: I think it was a good discussion.
Thanks, everyone, for sharing your opinions.
Let's talk more deeply next time.
That topic is very controversial.
People's opinions are sharply divided.
I want to stay neutral.
Facts matter more than emotions.
You should hear the other person out fully.
grammar: 상대방 (sangdaebang) = the other party; 끝까지 = to the end.

english: We should lend an ear to opposing views too.
grammar: 귀를 기울이다 = to lend an ear: 귀를 기울여요.

english: In a debate you must be polite.
Please don't misunderstand me.
A grounded argument is persuasive.
We need diverse perspectives.
There is no single right answer to this.
We should try to understand each other.
grammar: -려고 = in order to: 이해하려고 노력해요 = try to understand.

english: We shouldn't make the decision hastily.
I back that opinion.
grammar: 지지하다 = to support/back: 지지해요 (jijihaeyo).

target: 이 논의는 시간이 좀 걸릴 것 같아요.
english: This discussion will probably take a while.
Each person has their own stance.
grammar: 각자 (gakja) = each; 자기 (jagi) = ones own.

english: We must find a better direction.
Cooperation yields better results.
We need alternatives more than criticism.
Good questions make good discussions.
grammar: 만들다 keeps ㄹ before -어: 만들어요 (mandeureoyo) = makes.
